correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2 and real t>0, strict positivity gives unique symmetric scaling. Two exact row equations reduce scaling to a monotone scalar c(t); the matrix decomposes into a one-dimensional hub contrast plus m-1 leaf differences. Differentiating the full log-factor sweep gives B^2 and the two exact crossing values c1=1/(m+2), c2=(m+2)/(m^2+2m+2). Their ordered signs prove a globally unique t-optimal robust local factor m^2/(m^2+2m+2)^2. The exact post-second-normalization hub residual factorizes as mt((m-1)t-m)(mt^2-m-1) over an everywhere-positive denominator, proving precisely two possible immediate finite resonances; the primary full-text Cohen–Nathanson theorem rules out any later finite completion. Bundled verify.py passes 5605 finite assertions, but those do not replace proofs of universal claims. The local factor and finite initialized orbit are intentionally distinct quantities.

originality.rationale: The generalized singular-value rate principle (Knight 2007) and universal at-most-two termination result (Cohen–Nathanson 2019) are both credited and not claimed new. Inspected full-text literature establishes these generic ingredients but not the explicit three-mode rate switches, unique tunable hub affinity, or two exact parameter resonances and their rate comparison on the given hub–clique kernel. Semantic claims searches found differing binary and unbalanced scaling results but no implication covering the complete present joint theorem. The conclusion remains contingent on unindexed literature and human publication-priority review.
residual_risks: The claim has been checked against the available primary works and semantic index, not every publication. An unindexed exactly equivalent one-parameter tuning or stronger family theorem may exist.
Some near-neighbor results are accessible as indexed descriptions rather than full manuscripts. Those descriptions alone were not used to certify that their whole manuscripts lack stronger coverage.
The special matrix A_m(t) is a natural simplified family; the result does not generalize without further work to all positive hub-clique affinity matrices.

value.rationale: The precise motivational gap is choosing a positive hub-to-clique affinity that minimizes the full local worst-direction Sinkhorn convergence factor, not merely a symmetric initialization rate. The nontrivial (m-1)-dimensional leaf-difference eigenmode introduces two exact mode switches and a uniquely optimal t; the two resonance parameters isolate when starting from the original unscaled matrix gives exact finite termination, and the closed-form rate ratio explains an unusual performance trade-off. This is an exact natural matrix-family classification rather than an arbitrary enumerated example or one-step textbook calculation. The narrow kernel family and exact arithmetic are disclosed.
